messages:
alex: heads-up — customer reported a surge where many client jobs retried simultaneously after a heartbeat reset, ended up with lots of 429s and a few duplicate ops. seeing this with SDK v1.3.2 defaults.

mayra: can you paste minimal repro + logs? which endpoints and payload sizes?

alex: short repro: heavy batch of ~120 concurrent requests, each using the SDK default retry policy (maxRetries=5, base=100ms, expo=true, jitter=true). after ~30s the customer network briefly flapped and the client lib emitted a heartbeat reset -> connection closed. lots of clients then immediately retried. relevant log excerpt:

```
2026-02-18T12:07:10.123Z client: heartbeat reset, seq=42
2026-02-18T12:07:10.125Z request: POST /v1/generate  id=abc123 status=429 retry-after not present
2026-02-18T12:07:10.127Z retry: scheduling retry #1 delay=0.098s (expo+jitter)
2026-02-18T12:07:10.230Z request: POST /v1/generate  id=def456 status=429
2026-02-18T12:07:10.231Z retry: scheduling retry #1 delay=0.045s (expo+jitter)
```

jen (support): ah — small delays before retries means many clients retry within the same slot -> throttle amplifies. do we set idempotency keys for these requests? if not, duplicates are possible.

alex: customers are using idempotency for billing-critical paths, but this workload is mixed (some non-idempotent background jobs). main ask: how to recommend changes to prevent retry storms when heartbeat resets happen?

dmitri: two angles — client-side and server-side. client-side quick wins: 1) increase base backoff to 250-500ms for high-concurrency batch workloads, 2) enable server-aware backoff (honor Retry-After header), 3) add small fixed jitter window (avoid too small delays rounding to zero), 4) for non-idempotent ops, reduce maxRetries to 1 or disable automatic retries.

dmitri: also add a short randomized delay tied to client instance id, e.g. delay = base * (1 + rand(0..1)) * instance_index_hash_modN, so not everyone retries at once after a network blip.

mayra: any SDK config snippet we can share quickly?

alex: pasted local patch we applied to reproduce mitigation:

```
// SDK retry config patch
retryConfig: {
  maxRetries: 2,
  baseMs: 300,
  exponential: true,
  jitter: 'full',
  honorRetryAfter: true,
  instanceSalt: process.env.INSTANCE_ID || 'unknown',
}
```

alex: plus we added an early-idempotency wrapper for non-critical tasks: if no idempotency key present, we attach a client-generated guid and server ignores it for non-billing routes.

jen (support): good. on the server side we can also improve: emit Retry-After on short bursts or return 503 with Retry-After for capacity-shedding so clients don't immediately hammer. also we can expose a per-customer queueing suggestion metric in Console.

ops-bot: ticket created TKT-7421 — assigned to eng-runtime for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

dmitri: one caveat — don't rely on heartbeat header alone to gate retries. some clients may treat connection resets as transient and retry aggressively. recommend shipping an SDK default change: bump base to 250ms and default maxRetries to 2 for batch/concurrent methods. also add a note in release notes about idempotency guidance.

mayra: i'll draft a short support KB with repro steps, the sdk config snippet, and recommended server headers. alex can you attach the customer's minimal repro script and approximate token counts?

alex: done — uploaded repro gist and token counts to the ticket. repro includes a small Docker compose that spawns 150 workers hitting /v1/generate.

jen (support): thanks — marking this as "actionable guidance". we'll recommend: (1) idempotency for billing paths, (2) reduce retries for non-idempotent tasks, (3) increase base backoff + full jitter, (4) server Retry-After for capacity shedding.

alex: tl;dr: burst + heartbeat reset -> simultaneous tiny-delay retries -> amplified 429s. fix with slightly larger base delay + jitter + fewer retries + idempotency where needed.

jen (support): closing thread here, will follow up in the ticket with KB link. :slightly_smiling_face:
